description:
crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver has no gas phase in its type system.

- Material enum (src/lib/boussinesq_thermophysical_properties/mod.rs:14) has exactly 2 variants: Solid(SolidMaterial), Liquid(LiquidMaterial).
- LiquidMaterial (:126) has 7 variants: TherminolVP1, DowthermA, HITEC, YD325, FLiBe, FLiNaK, CustomLiquid(...). All six named fluids are single-phase heat-transfer oils or molten salts. No steam, water, water-vapour or air.
- SolidMaterial (:58) has 5 variants: SteelSS304L, Copper, Fiberglass, PyrogelHPS, CustomSolid(...).
- Crate-wide greps for GasMaterial, enum Gas, Material::Gas, VapourMaterial, SteamMaterial, LiquidMaterial::Steam return ZERO hits in src/. Greps for gas|vapou?r|superheat|two-phase|quality in the thermophysical-properties module return zero.

This is architecturally consistent -- the crate is named *Boussinesq*, i.e. incompressible single-phase by construction -- so treat it as a SCOPE BOUNDARY, not an oversight. But the practical consequence is real: MELCOR-style control-volume hydrodynamics (non-condensable gases, vapour/liquid pools, phase change) has no representation here, and adding one means a new Material arm plus every match site updated. Under the workspace no-trait-objects/enum-dispatch rule that is a breaking change to a published enum.

Decision needed from the maintainer: extend tuas, or build CVH in a separate lumped-parameter crate (see the MELCOR-lite epic) and leave tuas single-phase.

Verified 2026-08-07 against the working tree.
title: tuas: no gas phase in the Material type system — blocks MELCOR-style CVH

description:
Source: docs/real-time-multifidelity-scoping.md (written 2026-08-07; self-labelled "scoping analysis, not an approved plan", AI-assisted draft, not human-reviewed; audited against develop at 8c9ddd05).

VERDICT THE DOC REACHES: exactly one fidelity band runs in real time today and it is the lowest one -- lumped/system TH plus point kinetics, measured on CIET v2 at 94.7 s simulated in 94.7 s wall-clock, 27 ms median compute per 100 ms step (27% duty cycle). The gap to the next rung is ~3 orders of magnitude and does NOT close by optimisation. Design rule: a band that cannot meet its deadline is not allowed in the loop -- it goes offline and its output becomes a table.

TWO LEADING FINDINGS: (1) the crate literally named "real-time process control simulator" is the one component whose per-step cost is UNBOUNDED, and it is still in TUAS's PID path; (2) nothing in the workspace is a surrogate or ROM -- raffles/src/surrogate.rs is 54 lines of doc comment and zero code. There is also NO benchmarking infrastructure anywhere (no criterion, no benches/).

RECOMMENDED ARCHITECTURE: generalise what tampines' fhr_sim_v2 already does -- enum-dispatched fidelity levels on wall-paced threads at separate rates sharing Arc<RwLock<PlantState>>, with conservation-asserting state handoff. KEY SEQUENCING INSIGHT: snapshot/restore must come FIRST, because fidelity switching is a state-serialisation problem in disguise; doing it after the FidelityLevel enum means building it twice.

PHASE 1 is making the band that already runs actually TRUSTWORTHY: remove the unbounded-cost control path, the live todo!() panic paths in the flagship FHR simulator, the ~40 IF97 panic sites that kill the physics thread, and the two pacing defects; and stand up a criterion harness so any of it is measurable.
PHASE 2 is the capability: snapshot/restore/backtrack, then a FidelityLevel enum with conservation-asserted handoff, then a reduced circulating-fuel PRKE demonstrated against moltres.

DONE = a wall-clock-paced simulator sustaining >= 1.0x real-time factor with <= 200 ms control-to-response latency UNDER LOAD (not idle), whose per-step cost is bounded and measured by a committed benchmark baseline per band, that can snapshot and restore plant state, and that can switch fidelity at a timestep boundary with total mass and energy asserted conserved BY TEST.

Everything here remains an OFFLINE DEMONSTRATION ONLY -- never an operational digital twin, never plant monitoring.

DO NOT FILE AS DECIDED PLAN (the doc's own flags):
- The >= 1.0x / 200 ms / 20 Hz figures in section 3.2 are self-labelled ENGINEERING JUDGEMENT, "not values taken from a cited standard". Whether an ANSI/ANS-3.5 anchor is obtainable at all is OPEN, because ANS-3.5 validation needs reference-plant data DATA_POLICY.md forbids. Do not file them as requirements.
- MSRE-first CONTRADICTS docs/reactor-scoping/README.md:120-133, which recommends finishing the FHR widget migration first. That is a maintainer decision; the two docs must be reconciled.
- The bedok seam is gated on an OPEN DECISION (is bedok the neutronics path?), not ready to file as approved work. Until that call is made the nodal-diffusion band cannot even be costed -- it has never executed.
- Do NOT file a raffles::surrogate implementation issue. The doc explicitly says: do not block real-time work on raffles; build surrogates as tabulated offline coefficients and physics-form reduced models in the crates that own the physics. Neural surrogates are recommended AGAINST (auditability posture, no training data).
- Nine explicitly-undetermined items in section 7 must not be cited as facts, notably: the LOADED CIET step cost (unmeasured; the 27 ms is the IDLE state and is "certainly higher" under load); any bedok timing (the 76.5 s figure is Octave running the original MATLAB, not the Rust port); whether CIET v2 physics matches v1 (port-equivalence V&V op-wqk.13.6 has NOT been run -- v2 is "a faithful port of validated physics", not "validated"); Android/Termux real-time behaviour (compile proxy only); all GUI claims (no display available).
- The full tuas_boussinesq_solver suite was NOT run and its pass state is unreliable by construction: 46 #[ignore]d tests plus ~48 more with the #[ignore] commented out by hand.
- All [M] timings are machine-specific to the maintainer's box; re-measure before citing.
title: Real-time multi-fidelity simulator loop: make the low band solid first
